pos.text:
Usually I don’t really write reviews, but this game is special. As a full time working dad my time is very limited. However, this game reignited the love that I felt for games in a period where time was available in abundance, and your time was respected by developers. Furthermore, it reminds me of a time where the world seemed more simple, and devs still cared about their art before shareholders and marketeers dictated the course of development of a game.

The game embraces old school jrpg vibes whilst it does not take itself too seriously. The characters are light hearted but serious when required during certain phases of story telling. I find them engaging and above all courageous. The overall story is quite simple but that is certainly not a bad thing, it’s well put together.

The combat system is simple but in depth enough to keep me hooked. The lock system is a clever way to ensure

Okay, "Yes I recommend," IF you love Chrono Trigger, because that's what this is all about.  If you aren't looking for a "love letter to CT and other early Squaresoft," you may find this a little saccharine.  I played CT about 80 billion times when I was a kid and so this is absolutely working on the part of me that will always love and adore that game.  But I'm hearing people's complaints about Garl and...yea, I see it.  We'll see how it goes along, I haven't finished it yet.  But it looks/sounds absolutely lovely and the character sprites are very expressive and fun.  Having a great time with it.

My experience with Sea of Stars was... weird. First off, the game is gorgeous, it is bar none one of the most visually interesting games I’ve played. Everything else is a different story. The battle system, while unique, is a bit simple for my tastes, and I was sick to death of it by the time I got to the true ending. Though with a bit of expansion on the base concept, I think it stay engaging for longer. The story is very predictable if you are familiar with JRPGs, but that is not a crime. 

 I did fully finish the game and got the true ending because despite its flaws, Sea of Stars is undeniably a passion project. You can almost feel how much love was put into this game. This is best demonstrated in the Watchmaker DLC, which is disappointingly short, but otherwise solves almost every other issue with the game. I have [b]mixed feelings[/b] about this game, so [b]this won't be an entirely positive review[/b]. This game is [b]loved by most people[/b] who have played it, but I don't think it's that great. [b]It's not a bad game, tho[/b].

Sea of Stars is [b]perfect for people who have never played a JRPG[/b], or for those who want one without doing Excel math every turn.

[b]The art and soundtrack are undeniably beautiful[/b]. You can tell it's a game [b]made with love[/b].

[h1]Story[/h1]
In this world, [b]solstices[/b] sometimes bring about the [b]magical birth[/b] of warriors infused with the power of [b]sunlight[/b] or [b]moonlight[/b]. These are known as the [b]Solstice Warriors[/b].

Their purpose is to [b]protect the world from evil[/b], but since they aren't always born, [b]the world isn't always at peace[/b].

This time [b]Valere[/b] and [b]Zale[/b] are born, [b]the blandest and annoying

[b] Sea of Stars is a beautifully made RPG that brings together amazing pixel art, a memorable soundtrack, fun combat and a charming story to create a truly amazing adventure. Every part of the game feels carefully crafted, from its world and characters to its little details, making it an experience that every RPG fan should try.

A beautiful adventure! The pixel-art visual style is absolutely charming and gives the game a strong identity. The music is really enjoyable and truly enhances the feeling of traveling. There’s a wide variety of environments to explore, which makes the adventure feel even richer. As for the story, it took me much further than I initially expected.

To sum it up: it’s beautiful, fun to play, the world is inspired, and the playable characters are great. They have strong synergies, and everyone gets their moment to shine. It’s a game that puts a smile on your face, what more could you ask for?

I like this game but Garl is really pissing me off.

He leaves no room for character development due to him constantly interfering in conversations.
Otherwise, this game has a pretty artstyle and really good music. Combat gets a bit stale sometimes.
Luckily new side characters bring new skills, damage types and combos to the table.

I absolutely loved Sea of Stars. It's such a love letter to classic pixel adventures while maintaining its own identity.  The combat is really fun and the story keeps you hooked and adventuring. The team spent extra time adding more to the story and now we have the Sunset Edition. Finally complete. It's a little bittersweet. 

Either way, I HIGHLY recommend this game if you're looking for good story, fun combat, and some good ole pixel based nostalgia. They really nailed it.

Sea of Stars - 100% Completion Review
Score: 11/10

Sea of Stars is a RPG in the style of old gaming classics such as Golden Sun and Chrono Trigger that focuses on a group of friends as they accept their fate as the Children of Solstice and do their duty to defend the world from the evil Fleshmancer, after fully completing the game i'll give some pro's, neutrals and cons.

PRO'S:
-Good characters that are well written, well designed and stylish
-Great environments with amazing attention to detail
-Amazing lighting and effects that really give the game a nice mystic type of feel
-Good amount of puzzles that are well designed and fun to figure out
-Good combat that is unique, well designed and balanced
-Good music that fits the game perfectly, great soundtrack
-Great story that has plenty of twists and turns along with many good heartfelt moments
-Good map exploration that is very reminisc
Overall well made and good pacing. Story just ok, a bit of content. Character designs are good and combat is engaging for a JPRG.

First of all, I'll just say it straight out: I enjoyed it, a lot. That includes the DLC, which definitely ups the combat challenge by a decent amount.

In hindsight, though, the game really took me for a ride. My enjoyment started out neutral, climbed during the early game, then dropped hard around the midpoint as I grew increasingly frustrated with the timing mechanics. Once I finally mastered it - or at least became as accustomed to the combat as I could, my enjoyment shot back up and stayed there until the end.

The presentation certainly helped. The pixel art is great, the OST is decent, there's no need for grinding, and the various QoL features, especially those related to difficulty adjustment, were much appreciated. There are also quite a few references to classic JRPGs that I appreciated.

Would highly recommend this game to anyone who maybe hasn't experienced this genre of game before. 

- The pixel art is beautiful
- The music just sounds so nice
- There's a lot of difficulty customisation to make the game easier or harder
-  I enjoyed meeting all the characters you can play as (Main Protags fall short a little)

Not gonna lie, I thought the game was all visuals but boring at the beginning. But I was wrong!
The story's getting better and better. I love the features and mini games like Wheels. The puzzles are also so fun to solve. I never thought the map would be so complex.
As I said before, the visuals are amazing. Gorgeous pixelated game. They sure are paying attention to detail: animations, shadows, coloring. Beautifully done. 

Such a fun game, the type that makes me get lost in the game.

YES. If you miss old JRPGs from the SNES era, this is the perfect love letter to them. The pixel art is absolutely breathtaking, the music takes you back to the 90s and the combat, while still being turn based has its own fun mechanics that make it more dynamic, without being too hard to master. The story is more than good enough imo, as it keeps the essence of old RPGs but feels special with many memorable characters (not the protagonists, although they're there mostly to be the player's vessel, but they do get more development in the DLC) and many funny moments. I 100% it some months ago but I forgot to give it a review. In general, it is a game I hold close to my heart and again, if you like old JRPGs you will probaly like Sea of Stars a lot, so go give it a try!

I don't think a positive review is what this game really deserves, but it for sure is not thumbs down worthy.
I get what this game tries to do, but it falls short on every aspect, aside from the graphics, maybe.

Rpg elements are really barebones, stats are basic and have very little depth.
Dialogues and story feel pretty average, nothing stands out (Characters or events)
Combat is alright. Again, not much depth to it, but it compensates with good difficulty and quick time events such as parries and power ups.
Hated the backtracking.

In the end this is a very forgettable game which, however, you'll still enjoy playing. 6.5/10

[h1]A modern RPG with an old-school soul[/h1]
This game is genuinely awesome - I absolutely love this kind of pixel art style. The combat system stays fun throughout thanks to the different abilities and attacks you gradually unlock, and the various characters all bring something unique to the party. I also liked that the battles constantly keep you paying attention instead of just mindlessly selecting attacks. The story is enjoyable, the achievements are actually worth chasing since many of them unlock meaningful gameplay elements, and the free DLC is a nice bonus that rounds out the whole package really well. I ended up spending 36 hours getting 100%, and honestly, I enjoyed the entire journey. Easy recommendation for anyone who loves classic-style RPGs ⚔️✨🎮!
Visually gorgeous, addicting gameplay, and pure entertainment. Easily one of the best experiences I’ve had recently

I haven't played a couch co-op game this good in a very long time. 

Solid story, beautiful artwork, fun combat, and a ton of plot twists even a veteran gamer didn't see coming. A great game for friends or spouses to join in on. reminds me of games such as Golden Sun, Breath of Fire and earlier Final Fantasy games. 10/10
A good story about best friends going on a humble adventure, seeing the world, and growing old. I enjoyed it.

YAH! YAH! YAH! YAH! YAH! YAH! YAH! YAH! YAH! YAH! YAH! YAH! YAH! YAH! YAH! YAH! 

As of writing this, this is the best pixel styled game I've played. Plus! The moments where it decides NOT to be pixel art was an even better surprise every time it occurred. Love it when games have a mile of diversity within style / art-style, shifting up the visuals, time to time, is awesome.

Gulgul is one of the funniest enemies I've ever seen in a video game LOL

What a phenomenal experience

Sea of Stars builds upon the already solid foundation that Sabotage established with The Messenger and adds a wonderful RPG journey through beautifully rendered worlds filled with fun NPCs, fantastic music and well thought out designs.

When I finally finished this game last night, I felt as if I'd just had a warm dessert, was tucked in and even got to say thank you to the devs themselves. This is a great game that will leave you feeling warm and fuzzy inside. There's a lot of fun to be had, the combat is very enjoyable and there's a lot to explore and do! 

If you've a week off and want to intermittently fill it with a whimsical RPG centered on the love between friends and their dedication to fighting evil, please give Sea of Stars a try! And whilst you're at it, try the Messenger out too for a completely different genre experience! Both are absolutel

* If you try to break locks, to usually have to save your abilities/empowered attacks to be able to do that in the number of turns provided. Enemies also take reduced damage while channeling locked abilities (60% reduced in my game). So you’re encouraged to save all your strongest damaging abilities for when enemies take the least damage, making fights a slow awful grind.

This game is like Chrono Trigger was combined with the Mario & Luigi games.

For most of the time playing I felt rather conflicted as I enjoyed the visuals and the world that was built up around it. But the parts that I disliked grew more prominent with each passing hour.

- One of the worst stories I have seen in a game, bad enough to make me angry with how the ending was handled.
- Plot twists occur with zero foreshadowing only to then immediately move on
- Subpar characters that try to seem deeper than they actually are.
- There is a certain character the game glazes and treats like a saint, they are never in the wrong and everything goes right for them. The biggest contrivences in the plot are because of them.
- Almost zero variety in the combat system as every character only gets 3 skills, you will be using skills most since they don't take an eternity to charge.
- Ok at best music

The setting, the combat, the level design, the music, the sprite work oh my god - but despite getting to the late game, I never finished it, and I don't really feel any desire to whatsoever despite all the things about it that hypothetically I should have loved. 

In spite of a thousand little things that should work in its favor, the game is ultimately just kind of boring. Despite so much of the game being incredible in a void, there's so little personality to so much of it that it feels like a waste of time. Lots of mixed opinions that make it hard to recommend this game. If you grew up with a lot of the RPG classics, then this game is very appealing on the surface. The beautiful visuals are definitely the best part of the game, with vibrant colors and dynamic lighting. The music is also solid. Exploration is also good and varied because there are a few abilities you can use to navigate the environments and interact with puzzles. That's about it for the positives.
The combat is a mixed experience. It's turned based combat but has active timed commands similar to older games like Super Mario RPG and Paper Mario. It's fun at first, but it gets tedious and repetitive due to how this game progresses. The characters get very few skills and while there are combination skills between party members, there's not a lot of them either and they take time to build up during combat to be able to be used.

This game is the biggest bait in jrpg history.  It looks pretty but looks are deceiving.  The story goes nowhere for... literally the entire early game.  I've never seen such cool character concepts be so dull, and the combat has no variety at all.  I can appreciate well thought out simplicity, but after using moonerang for the 80th time...  And just when I thought the story might do something interesting, I was given a hand wave with the "power of friendship..." again...

Seriously, just go play Chrono Trigger.  This ain't it.  Or if you want to play something new, try out Chained Echoes.  It isn't perfect, but it at least dared to be creative.
Beautiful game, wonderful soundtrack but the story is really weak, the cast of characters unappealing, the combat repetitive. I really tought it could be the next Chrono Trigger :(

This game is as shallow and lacking in characterization as it is beautiful. Like a siren calling to you from a rock in the sea it promises to give you the same depth in gameplay as Golden Sun and same quality of story as Chrono Tigger of old. When you take a closer look you instead find an incredibly mediocre and cookie-cutter story with flat characters that could only hold up in a tv show for children aged 4-6 and gameplay that will make you bored enough to tear your hair out.

I really wish it was different because the visuals are stunning, but looks are not everything...

All in all this game was a disappointment.

[*]The fighting mechanics, the combos and such are really fun and deserve lots of praise.
[*]Graphic/World design is, even though 2.5D games are getting somewhat boring, very nice and pretty.
[*]Sound design and music are also top tier 
[*]The bonus missions or storys for the playable characters were short and fun. 
[/list]

However the bad aspects of this game...
[list]
[*]The story might be one of the worst I have ever seen in a serious JRPG. It wasn't just one thing but a combination of the further points that made it boring, cringe and often just plain up bad.
[*]I really disliked the characters, both the main protagonists as well as the NPCs
[list]
[*]Valere and Zale are boring 2 dimensional characters whos personality doesn't matter and could easily be replaced
[*]Garl was nothing but annoying

This game really suffers from bad writing.  The game looks really good, but the story, characters, and combat should have been thought out more.  It was such a slog to get through, and this is coming from someone who loved the games this is based on.  Also the lack of wrap up with the ending is sad.

Fantastic visuals and sounds. Combat stars out alright but gets monotonous after a while. There was actually a lot I liked about this game, and would recommend it if not for the writing.

It is rare for me to play a game with characters that I really dislike. Usually if I think the writing is this bad, I just uninstall right away. However, the other parts of the game was clearly made with such love that I harboured a hope that I just needed to get to the next plot beat, and it would finally be good. Just move a little further, and the writers will lock in, give us some good scenes that actually makes me care even the slightest about these people, and then keep on trodding along at a mediocre pace, carried by all the other aspects of the game.

And for all I know, that might still happened. Maybe 10 hours is the magic number, or 20. But I put 6 hours of my life into this game, and the cha

How does a game nail the visuals but completely miss on the combat and story? It's a 40 hour game with literally the same combat from the tutorial until the end.

Also whoever wrote Garl as a character should never work as a writer again.

So here's the thing with sea of stars, gameplay wise it doesn't do anything wrong unfortunately it also doesn't do anything to stand out from the pack. Nowadays the JRPG market has had a million good/great titles and this in no way reinvents the wheel which wouldn't be a problem if the story was very good however it is not.

a lot of the story beats kind of go along for no reason, and the final nail in this is that ending is a total let down. In this day and age for a jrpg or jrpg inspired game you either need to have stellar gameplay or at the least a stellar story if you drop the ball on both you end up with something mid in a market that is pretty saturated.

Sea of Stars was a game that I had on my wishlist for a long time and was excited for, after hearing it was positioning itself as something of a spiritual successor to the JRPGs of my childhood, like Chrono Trigger, FFVI and Super Mario RPG. In some ways, it is. It certainly has the look and sound - the graphics, animations and music are excellent. After that, the game barely compares.
  
The battle system mostly combines Chrono Trigger's skill combos with Super Mario RPG's timed button press system, though characters don't learn nearly the variety of moves as in those games, so what you end up doing in the first hours of the game isn't far removed from what you're doing in the final hours. There's also a lock system - essentially a way to reduce or negate enemy spells by hitting them with the right combination of attacks - but I found that much of the time breaking the lock was either n

This game is so boring that it's impressive. Combat barely gets any deeper after the tutorial to the point where a toddler could master it. Story is lame and cringe. The devs constantly push you to love Garl, but he is just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ annoying. The two main characters have less character than a silent main protagonist. The pacing is ♥♥♥♥. The puzzles are constant and irritating. 

The game is beautiful and the music is nice, but that's the only two things going for it. 

3/10

Edit: Okay its not as bad as I was saying. Problems are still there, but a 3/10 was a bit harsh.

4.5/10
The world is beautiful, but the story is dull, and the combat, repetitive. I might have liked this when I was younger, but I don't have the patience for it these days.

I love classic JRPGs. I have an SNES and Sega CD library full of physical copies of games, and an even broader collection on PC. I couldn’t get past a few hours into this game. I wanted to love this game, but couldn’t. I was looking forward to starting this game for months based on the descriptions and presentation of gameplay. I don’t get to dive into RPGs as often as I used to, and I was hoping for that classic, childlike feeling going in to a pixel RPG like I was 10 years old again.

I did not find that feeling here.

There’s a lot to like about this game. The graphical style is well done, The combat is for the most part enjoyable. But the story! Oh man, the story is where it all falls apart. 

The characters themselves are all wishy washy generic templates, with almost no depth, if any depth at all. This includes the two main protagonists, who’s hero’s journey as of the third dungeon
The world and art is absolutely gorgeous, but the story is bland and the characters uninteresting. The art only kept me going for so long.

The puzzles are constant and irritating. 

The game is beautiful and the music is nice, but that's the only two things going for it. 

3/10

Edit: Okay its not as bad as I was saying. Problems are still there, but a 3/10 was a bit harsh.

4.5/10

The gameplay is good, the setting is thematic, the "charm" is there, and the emotional beats hit; but the story... the story just ain't there mate. The main story is passable if you just want a game to pass the time with, but throes of the watchmaker is one of the worst stories I've seen, especially so as it relates to the main game, plus the gameplay takes a hit. If you don't care about a story that won't resonate, that you won't remember even a month later, then this game's pretty good. I however cannot give it a positive review because I played this game multiple times to 100% collectables and do some achievements (before they added multiplayer achievements, effectively barring me from 100% achievements), and I can't even give you a plot synopsis.

This is one of those games I didn’t fully complete before reviewing, but Sea of Stars: Sunset Edition has so much content that finishing everything can easily take more than 40–60 hours. Since I’ve already reached the end credits, though, I feel I’ve seen enough to give the game a proper review.

As I mentioned, the game is simply too long for me. Even after completing most of it and collecting all 60 Rainbow Conches, there’s still plenty of content left. The bigger problem is that the systems start to feel very repetitive, especially as you get deeper into the game.

Take food, for example. Most food items are essentially about increasing HP and MP (e.g., either +10 HP or +20 HP or +5 HP, but with 5 MP). During combat, you can only use one food item per turn, so you’ll naturally pick the strongest one. Outside of combat, the differences barely matter.

Weapons and armor are even simpler

Its almost very good, but instead becomes a game few finish. Visually it's gorgeous, and feels good to play. Mechanically the combat is clunky, unfun, and often just completely against you.  Each battle expects you at full resources, which results in a lot of walks back to the camp after a single fight. regular moves can reduve 70% of your health and you are encouraged to not use any moves until one of these deadly 'locks' appears...
The combat lock system is supposed to reward you for clever order of play, but instead it becomes an (often impossible) goal to chase just to stay alive. 2 enemies gain lock moves that will take 3 specialized (resource consuming)attacks to remove, each with a 2 move countdown, and those moves will easily completely kill 1 or 2 characters???
They added a lot of optional modifyers to how the game and combat works to try to tweak the 'difficulty' but honestly t

The art, music, map/puzzle design are all fantastic, you basically try to get through the maps by solving various puzzles which is about 60% of the game and really fun. 
The rest 40% is related to combat and kinda meh tbh. 
tldr
My biggest issue is the turn system where every enemy gets a turn when one of your character act. You have 3 char slot and can freely swap chars but each one can only act once per party round. This means for each of your party round every enemy gets 3 turns which doesn't make sense. It also goes against the lock breaking feature where you have to perform a combo of attack types to stop a big enemy attack. You will often get into situations where your first char just acted and an enemy starts charging an attack that only your first char can break, and you can't do anything since the charge complete in 2 turns and you can't use the first char until 2 more char acte

Sure it's fun and unique battle system and the art is really beautiful, however I was disappointed - it's pretty underwhelming and the story is pretty mid - not exciting all the way to the final battle. I expect a few twist here and there but nope.. the journey is too easy and one way. the world map is rather small.

reviews.title: Great port, please add 1-handed support
reviews.text: I adore this game & played it on steam. Quickly bought the port and am adoring it. Very elegant controls. My one request would be to allow either side of the screen to be touched in order to select/dragged to use the d-pad; regardless of what side of the screen you touch. I know many other mobile ports that allow for this. Or perhaps a way to switch sides in the menu? I recently suffered a hand injury and cannot play video games with a regular controller until I heal. I am so grateful I can play SoS on mobile now, as it is actually a platform I can play video games on while my arm is injured. But it would be so much easier for me if I didn’t have to reach across either side of the screen every time I wanted to move/talk/jump/attack. A small inconvenience that I can handle, but it would surely increase accessibility for me and for many others with more permanent limb differences. Thank yo

The graphics are colorful and surprisingly well detailed. Done in what I’d say is reminiscent of 32-bit pixel games, but the level of shading and environmental animations bring a depth to the world. 

The story and characters are your standard JRPG fare, but if you’re into these games that’s not a negative, it’s just saying that part isn’t new or extra creative.

I had trouble at first figuring out what the battle instructions meant when saying to hold a particular button to enhance the attack, because the icon doesn’t look like any visible buttons on the screen, then I realized it meant to just press and hold the screen. It’s more obvious on the male character’s sun ball attack than on the female character’s Luna attacks. And blocking to reduce damage seems more ch

At its core, the game delivers a beautifully balanced turn-based combat system that never feels stale. reviews.title: Incredible adventure, well made port
reviews.text:
This is a must play for any RPG fans. It has a great story (especially if you’ve played The Messenger). The combat system is incredibly satisfying, be it through perfectly timed hits, or the strategic options that live mana opens up. 

As for the port itself, the touch controls feel very natural. You’re never required to hold more than one button at once (movement circle not counting as a button), so you don’t have to hold the phone awkwardly. There’s controller support too, so you can use the original controls. My only gripe is that I wish you could switch the confirm/cancel buttons on a controller layout. It’s not really an issue, since I can just change that in the phone settings, but it’d be nice I could do it in a way that didn’t also change the button labels.

reviews.title: Smooth, Polished, and Fun
reviews.text:
Sea of Stars has been an absolute joy so far. About five hours in, and it already feels like a love letter to classics like Chrono Trigger and Super Mario RPG, two of my all-time favorites. The combat, exploration, and overall vibe hit that same nostalgic sweet spot while still feeling fresh.

The humor lands, the music is fantastic, and everything just comes together in a really polished way. I’ve also been especially impressed with the Relics system, which lets you tailor the difficulty to your preference. Some make the game more forgiving (like automatically healing after battles so you don’t have to constantly manage menus), while others add extra challenge. It’s a great approach that makes the game more accessible without taking away from the core experience.

The mobile version itself is very well done. The touch controls feel natural and responsive, and I haven’t experienced any i

reviews.title: Controls and saving

Even if you make an option to swap it that won’t solve the problem. It’s an easy fix that the devs absolutely can do with little effort. This is the main issue but also you need to make the game auto save all the time. In a game like this you easily lose a half hour of playtime if you get interrupted because the game closes if minimized even briefly. Anyway this is one of my favorite games and the 3rd time I’ve bought it, so please please fix these extremely minor yet extremely major qol issues. Love you guys

reviews.title: Cool Port; Aspect Ratio Shortcoming
reviews.text: A great RPG and generally a well done port by Playdigious. One issue for me, though, and I bring it up here only because the game’s product page doesn’t: the aspect ratio presented here is a severely letterboxed version on iPad (and I assume iPhone too, although to a lesser degree). There’s been no attempt to provide an option to reframe or zoom visuals to fit the aspect ratio of your device. As long as you’re okay with less gameplay real estate, the game is still great. But hopefully 1) they address this; and 2) they clearly let buyers know what they are and are not getting.

But the UI for settings is a bit clunky, you have to click around too much just to get 5 items to adjust, and aside from settings, when you try to skip a cutscene, the game takes a second to register both fingers before loading the next scene. Otherwise, aside from these two issues, amazing game.

On top of that, an option to enable saves from anywhere. I can’t always play long enough to get to a save point and the game will close in the background, requiring a re-play of sections.

reviews.title: Obra maestra del Pixelart
reviews.text:
Sea of Stars es uno de los mejores juegos Pixelart que he jugado nunca.

El juego se siente vivo, te envuelven sus escenarios con el arte, los colores y la iluminación. Un detalle “tonto” que me sorprendió y habla muy bien del nivel de detalle es que en una cueva habían unas columnas verdes de cristal, al pasar por detrás los personajes no solo se difuminaron sutilmente, también se distorsionó su forma y se iluminaron del mismo color, tal como sucede con el vidrio. Lo que hicieron con pixeles me parece imposible de superar…

Además la historia es increíble, nunca sabes qué esperar en la próxima misión y tiene bastante contenido. Llevo ya 22h de juego pero creo que no he superado ni el 50% de la historia.

Y la música, la música es INCREIBLE. Súbanle el volumen al máximo porque se lo merece. Recuerdo entrar a la Isla Espectral, ir a la taberna del pueblo, y quedarme como 15 min escuchando

reviews.title: Just buy it! (First time player)
reviews.text:
Gorgeous graphics, fun and easy to follow story. It’s my first time and I found myself just stopping to admire the scenery honestly. It’s flipping beautiful. It just feels cozy. Only an hour in, but I can guarantee that $9 is BEYOND well worth. ALSO, major thanks to the crazy cool coders working on this game- they fixed a soft lock bug EXTREMELY fast (<1day). This is a company that listens to their fans, fixes bugs, and doesn’t waste time. Love, love. Take my money. Take my damn heart atp. 

PS: I know there are mixed reviews for this game generally. People say the characters are 1D (no personality), the writing is bad, the story is generic or unfulfilling. My two cents? Well, Im not done, I just started, but I can see some of these critiques; HOWEVER, I dont agree. My opinion: why cant we just have a fun story with simple writing, big moments, and light hearted characters who dont talk
